samples.xml_description:
<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Edge detection for a slowly changing 1-bit signal.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <enum id="state" width_description="[1:0]">
            <enum_value id="IDLE" value="2'b00">Idle state.</enum_value>
            <enum_value id="RISE" value="2'b01">Rise state.</enum_value>
            <enum_value id="DOWN" value="2'b10">Down state.</enum_value>
        </enum>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <reg id="state" type="sequential_logic">Current state.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" type="combinational_logic">Next state.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The edge_detect module detects rising and falling edges in the input signal a and generates corresponding output signals rise and down. 
        The module uses a finite state machine (FSM) with three states: IDLE, RISE, and DOWN. 
        In the IDLE state, the module checks for changes in the input signal a. If a rising edge is detected, the state transitions to RISE, and if a falling edge is detected, the state transitions to DOWN. 
        In the RISE state, the rise output signal is set to 1, and in the DOWN state, the down output signal is set to 1. 
        The state transitions occur on the positive edge of the clock signal clk, and the output signals rise and down are reset to 0 in the IDLE state.
    </implementation>
</module>
